name: Hardware-Assisted Projected Tetrahedra Rendering
definition: A volume rendering technique for unstructured data that uses hardware-assisted texture mapping to perform interpolation between vertex colors and opacities, and integrates color for use with a volume rendering system. It addresses artifacts (Mach bands) from linear interpolation of opacity in the original Shirley-Tuckman algorithm by using a texture table for the exponential opacity function.
summary: Hardware-Assisted Projected Tetrahedra Rendering is a volume visualization technique that uses hardware texture mapping to perform non-linear opacity integration, eliminating Mach band artifacts found in linear interpolation methods.
